title.en: Prepare an analytical petty cash book

say.en: Tea for visitors, a courier, an auto fare: the chief cashier should not be disturbed for every 50 rupees. A petty cashier handles these small payments. In this lesson: Explain the imprest system.
Prepare an analytical petty cash book.

body.en: A petty cashier is given a fixed amount, called the *imprest*, at the beginning of a period, say ₹5,000 for a month. He makes small payments out of it and records them. At the end of the period the main cashier reimburses exactly the amount spent, so the petty cashier again starts with the full imprest.
body.kn: ಆರಂಭದಲ್ಲಿ ಚಿಲ್ಲರೆ ಕ್ಯಾಷಿಯರ್‌ಗೆ ನಿಗದಿತ ಮೊತ್ತ (ಇಂಪ್ರೆಸ್ಟ್) ನೀಡಲಾಗುತ್ತದೆ. ಅವಧಿಯ ಕೊನೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಖರ್ಚಾದಷ್ಟು ಮೊತ್ತವನ್ನು ಮರುಪಾವತಿಸಲಾಗುತ್ತದೆ.

title.en: On the board: Analytical petty cash book

say.en: The petty cashier gets an imprest of 5,000 for July and records each small payment.
Each payment goes in the total column and again in its analysis column.

On 1 August the main cashier reimburses exactly what was spent, restoring the imprest.

narration.en: Let us work this out step by step. The petty cashier of Hegde & Sons receives an imprest of ₹5,000 on 1 July. Payments in July: postage ₹450, stationery ₹820, cartage ₹600, refreshments ₹1,130, conveyance ₹700. Columns: Postage & Stationery, Cartage & Conveyance, Refreshments. Find the column totals, the balance and the reimbursement.

say.en: Let us work this out step by step. The petty cashier of Hegde & Sons receives an imprest of 5,000 rupees on 1 July. Payments in July: postage 450, rupees stationery 820, rupees cartage 600, rupees refreshments 1,130, rupees conveyance 700 rupees. Columns: Postage & Stationery, Cartage & Conveyance, Refreshments. Find the column totals, the balance and the reimbursement.
Postage & Stationery equals 450 plus 820 equals 1,270 rupees.
Cartage & Conveyance equals 600 plus 700 equals 1,300 rupees; Refreshments equals 1,130 rupees.
Total spent equals 1,270 plus 1,300 plus 1,130 equals 3,700 rupees; balance in hand equals 5,000 minus 3,700 equals 1,300 rupees.
On 1 August the main cashier reimburses 3,700, rupees restoring the imprest of 5,000 rupees.
So the answer is Spent 3,700 rupees; balance 1,300 rupees; reimbursement 3,700 rupees.
